title: TPA overview (cloud)
description: Home: every TPA area at a glance, read from Cloud Monitoring. Every panel reads Cloud Monitoring metrics: Google's own, and the log-based counters tpa-platform's catalogue defines, whose labels are a closed list. No panel reads a log line.

links.title: PagerDuty incidents
links.tooltip: Open incidents page through PagerDuty; this site cannot list them

options.content:
**Open incidents are in PagerDuty**, not here: [PagerDuty incidents](https://app.pagerduty.com/incidents). Every Cloud Monitoring alert policy in a TPA project pages through it (urgent ones as high urgency). Google's own list, per project: [app](https://console.cloud.google.com/monitoring/alerting/incidents?project=__TPA_APP_PROJECT_ID__) · [member records](https://console.cloud.google.com/monitoring/alerting/incidents?project=__TPA_PHI_PROJECT_ID__) · [CRM](https://console.cloud.google.com/monitoring/alerting/incidents?project=__TPA_CRM_PROJECT_ID__).

This site reads metrics only: Grafana's Cloud Monitoring datasource cannot list incidents. Every panel reads Cloud Monitoring metrics: Google's own, and the log-based counters tpa-platform's catalogue defines, whose labels are a closed list. No panel reads a log line.

panels.title: Uptime checks passing (24 h)
panels.description: Share of uptime checks that passed in the last 24 h, by host. @@E@@Each check reads `/health` on a public host (the portal, auth and api hosts) from three US regions: a pass is the service answering through the load balancer and Cloud Armor. An outage pages when more than one region fails.@@Beta's hosts are behind IAP, so a check passes only on Google's sign-in page: it proves the address, the certificate, Cloud Armor and IAP, never the service behind them (that is the 5xx and instance panels). An outage pages when more than one region fails.@@

panels.title: Scheduled runs: a successful run within each job's deadline
auth-publisher
panels.description: Successful executions of `auth-publisher` in the last 6 minutes: its missed-run deadline (3 minutes, about one and a half cadences) plus three, because Cloud Run's job metrics can arrive up to 180 s after the run. MISSED: none, so its `missed run` policy is open or about to be. Reads "paused" or "database stopped", in no colour, while `auth-db` is stopped on purpose (the service's TPA_PAUSED_JOBS, TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES).

panels.title: Requests (1 h)
panels.description: Requests Cloud Run answered in the last hour (web, tpa-api, model-gateway).

panels.title: 5xx (1 h)
panels.description: 5xx answers in the last hour. `canary-5xx` opens above 0.1% (and five); the urgent liveness policies when every answer for ten minutes was a 5xx. Reads "paused" or "database stopped", in no colour, while `auth-db` or `tpa-db` is stopped on purpose (the service's TPA_PAUSED_JOBS, TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES).

panels.title: p95 (1 h)
panels.description: tpa-api's own p95 time to answer (its request line, without the streams, the file transfers and the model-backed rows): `tpa-api-latency` opens above 2 s for ten minutes. Cloud Run's own p95 for web and tpa-api counts the desk's 40-second streams, so it is on the Portal & API page only.

panels.title: Error groups (24 h)
panels.description: Error groups of `errors` seen in the last 24 h: one per Cloud Run service or job and the counter's labels, the same group the new-group and spike policies read. The Errors page lists them. Reads "paused" or "database stopped", in no colour, while `auth-db` or `tpa-db` is stopped on purpose (the service's TPA_PAUSED_JOBS, TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES).

panels.title: Instances now
panels.description: Cloud Run instances per service. Zero is how a scale-to-zero service idles; a service kept warm with none is the urgent `no instance` policy.

panels.title: auth-db
panels.description: Cloud SQL's own signals for auth-db: `database/up` (the urgent `auth-db-down` pages below 1 for five minutes) and disk used (`auth-db-disk` at 85% for ten minutes). "database stopped": stopped on purpose between test sessions (beta's database_activation_policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing.
